Every half-integer boundary and adjacent float is exercised for all byte positions and modifiers, with deterministic full-word alias/guard/mask checks. Literal hardware captures now validate the computed reference independently of GoC. Byte conversion is loose/fallback-only; the separate architecture tests explicitly reject strict exact. The nibble reference is exact bounded dyadic encoding and all selected nibbles/unselected bits are checked. Integer quantization and byte preservation intentionally use exact comparisons rather than fuzzy floating comparison.
diagnostics: Hardware capture failures identify row/column/CPU. The retained DPP hardware digest now checks each result against the computed routing/quantization reference with CPU, EXEC, descriptor, modifier and lane context.

scope: FP16 field packing and FP32 byte packing across both architectures and wave widths. Reuses the separately hardware-anchored field and quantization references. Strict exact FP16 packing is accepted only for RDNA4, with a literal sNaN-quieting result; strict exact byte packing is rejected. Optional exact state returns unsupported without touching output, and loose calls preserve optional state. scope: Six integer/FP32 conversion operations in both widths, loose/fallback semantics. Hardware ordinary/DPP digests already compare individual outputs to the model. Masks, aliases, guards, Wave64 high lanes and optional-state preservation/rejection have dedicated checks. Exact comparisons intentionally test conversion rounding and integer results; this does not imply supported strict exact semantics, which validation rejects.
diagnostics: Hardware assertions now include CPU, EXEC, opcode, DPP descriptor, modifier variant and lane. Computed helpers already print input/result/mode and literal witnesses independently anchor rounding rules.

scope: Six conversions across RDNA3/RDNA4 and both widths. Numerical integration reuses the independent integer reference. scope: Six int32/FP32/FP64 conversions in both widths, loose/fallback only. scope: Six integer/FP16/FP32 conversion operations, both widths, loose/fallback only. scope: Six conversions across both architectures and widths. scope: FP32/FP64 exponent extraction, both architectures and widths. scope: FP32 mantissa extraction across both architectures and widths, loose and strict exact. scope: FP32/FP64 LDEXP in both widths, loose/fallback only. diagnostics: Computed checks use per-batch traces and literal boundaries; DPP hardware digest has independent reference companions. No new golden data is required.

scope: Both LDEXP formats, architectures and widths. Long-double power-of-two reference is combined with explicit guest input/output flushing and RDNA3 OMOD gating. scope: FP16 LDEXP and exponent extraction in both widths, loose/fallback only. scope: FP16 scaling/exponent extraction across both architectures and widths. Reuses the independently decoded half reference with explicit guest flush/OMOD/overflow rules. scope: Raw 16/32-bit moves, both widths. Direct field selection, sign-bit ABS/NEG and preservation of unselected halves give exact references without floating arithmetic. diagnostics: Hardware capture now identifies width, modifier, half selection and lane; CPU is scoped. Exhaustive half and per-lane DPP checks supplement the retained digest.

scope: Four relative-register move forms, both widths, plus ordinary MOV sign-modifier composition. diagnostics: Whole-file comparisons identify opcode, M0 and route; literal offset-limit cases expose bounds errors, and per-word sign-modifier checks identify width/opcode/modifier/route/word.

scope: Raw 16/32-bit swaps, relative swaps and PERMLANE64 in both widths. Independent before-image exchange and lane XOR32 mapping are exact field/routing references. scope: Scalar hardware-register access and mode updates for RDNA3/RDNA4. Independent per-bit insertion/extraction checks all register IDs and offset/width combinations against manual-defined writable fields, with privilege, reserved-bit preservation, clock halves and literal architecture differences. Retained gfx1201 MODE/EXCP_FLAG_USER capture digests anchor the per-bit model on captured inputs; this is not arbitrary numerical reverse engineering. Tests cover optional snapshots, null outputs, unavailable exact state, error precedence and unchanged outputs, plus host-control preservation while modifying guest MODE. Mode instructions run every available CPU selector; scalar register enumeration uses baseline. Exact raw register comparisons apply in loose semantics too.
diagnostics: Hardware read/write corpora now report register, seed, source pattern and field boundaries, and check each output independently before the retained group digest. Literal and exhaustive field tests supplement capture evidence.

scope: Constant true/false integer and floating CMP/CMPX predicates in both wave widths, all available CPU selectors and both semantics. Boolean constants filtered by EXEC and independently modeled DPP destination enablement give directly justified exact masks; no approximate floating arithmetic is involved. Null source operands demonstrate that inputs are not read. Tests cover upper lanes, empty EXEC, ignored supported modifiers, invalid flags with preserved results and unsupported 64-bit DPP. Floating exact optional state is explicitly unsupported (including precedence over empty EXEC and bad flags); loose requested state is preserved. These tests do not claim floating exception generation.
diagnostics: Per-mask assertions and DPP configuration diagnostics; explicit sentinel values expose partial writes on errors. No golden array or fuzzy comparison is needed for constant predicate masks.

scope: Six add/subtract/reverse-subtract operations with and without carry-in, both widths and both semantics. Unsigned 64-bit arithmetic independently derives 32-bit results, borrow/carry and saturation. Direct captured values and masks now validate this reference without depending on GoC; the DPP capture retains its hardware digest plus per-lane routed arithmetic checks. Deterministic mt19937 boundary/random streams, chained 64-bit word arithmetic, all CPU selectors, inactive-lane carry clearing, scalar/vector aliases, guards and zero-EXEC/error preservation are covered. diagnostics: Hardware output checks identify operation/CPU/clamp/EXEC/lane; DPP digest companions additionally identify source carry, route, host rounding and semantics. Existing masked-alias tests retain complete before-image comparisons.

scope: Four RDNA3/RDNA4 signed/unsigned wide MAD spellings in Wave32. scope: Four narrow-factor and four wide-result Wave64 MAD entry points. Bounded 64-bit arithmetic handles signed/unsigned 16/24-bit factors and explicit extension/clamp. Both semantics/all CPU selectors, all narrow half/clamp modes, DPP row masks, upper-lane EXEC, source/destination aliases and guards are exercised. scope: Thirty-five Wave64 add/subtract/multiply/select/ternary entry points. Both semantics/all CPU selectors cover every encoded half-selector/clamp combination, DPP where supported, row masks, upper/inactive lanes, aliases and destination guards. Input patterns combine integer boundaries and defined unsigned mixing; mode-dependent generation is deterministic but not an exhaustive Cartesian input/mode product. scope: Eight Wave64 SAD variants, both semantics with STRICT and every available CPU selector. Primary sweeps use loose semantics; literal full-precision overflow and cross-half witnesses now run both semantics with STRICT. scope: RDNA3 and RDNA4 nonconstant FP16/32/64 CMP/CMPX predicates, both wave widths. Bitwise sign/magnitude ordering with explicit NaN, signed-zero, input-flush and half-selection rules supplies exact predicate masks; RDNA4 predicate hardware evidence is in the separately reviewed float_compare family. Both semantics, every CPU selector, eight guest policies and all ABS/NEG/half modifiers are covered on boundary and deterministic mixed inputs. RDNA3 DPP includes aliased scalar results in upper source words. RDNA3 requested exact state is explicitly unsupported with atomic failure; RDNA4 reporting is separately covered in compare_exceptions. Reporting/nonreporting predicate results now both check the independent bitwise ordering model rather than only one another. scope: Nine RDNA4 FP32 ternary selections plus five RDNA3 spellings in Wave32/Wave64. scope: Legacy Wave32 binary FP16/32/64 and packed FP16 plus ten half/single ternary entry points. scope: Nine RDNA4 half ternary selections and five RDNA3 spellings, both wave widths. Sortable integer keys, nested selection and independently decoded double/half rounding model provide loose references. All half encodings for one input with deterministic other operands, boundary triples, 8192 modifiers, overflow selection, CPU selectors, masks, aliases and untouched halves are exercised. scope: Wave32 DPP integration for nine half ternary selections, loose-only. Two gfx1201 digests cover finite inputs and OMOD boundaries with per-lane reference checks. scope: Four cube operations on both architectures and wave widths. scope: FP32/64 DIV_FIXUP policy integration, RDNA3/RDNA4 and Wave32/Wave64. scope: FP32/64 DIV_FMAS on both architectures and widths. All CPU selectors, sequenced mt19937 draws, masks and overlapping split destinations are covered.
